# TCGA-OV follow-up time-axis audit

**Input:** `clinical.project-tcga-ov.2026-10-09.json` (608 cases)  
**Generated by:** `../../scripts/audit_followup_timeline.py`  
**Machine-readable output:** `../../data/processed/followup_timeline_audit.json`

## Time reference decision

The TCGA follow-up form says that when intervals are used, they begin at the date of initial pathological diagnosis. GDC's standardization documentation identifies follow-up timing as an interval from the study's index date. In the supplied JSON, `index_date` is `Diagnosis` for 587/608 cases; it is absent for 21 cases. Therefore this project treats `days_to_follow_up` as days since diagnosis only for records whose `index_date` is explicitly `Diagnosis`. The current trajectory baseline excludes the other 21 cases.

Sources: [TCGA Follow-up Form (PDF)](https://www.nationwidechildrens.org/-/media/nch/research/documents/tcga/head-and-neck-followup-form.ashx), [GDC clinical data standardization](https://gdc.cancer.gov/about-data/gdc-data-processing/clinical-data-standardization), [GDC submission best practices](https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data_Submission_Portal/Users_Guide/Best_Practices/).

## Data checks

- 1,720 follow-up records have `days_to_follow_up`; all values are integers in this export, ranging from 0 to 5,481, with no negative values.
- 1,151 non-Unknown disease-response records have a numeric follow-up day; one non-Unknown response lacks its day.
- Among patients with at least two timed non-Unknown response records, 80 have source-array entries that are not in increasing day order. The code sorts by day and does not trust JSON array order.
- No same-day group has conflicting known response labels. Duplicate labels at the same day are collapsed to one timepoint.
- After these rules, 118 cases have at least two distinct, unambiguous response timepoints, yielding 122 adjacent transitions for the first forecasting task.

## Manual spot checks

These examples were inspected directly in the supplied JSON. Identifiers are omitted here.

| Example | Source order (day: response) | Ordered timepoints | Check |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 1199: WT-With Tumor; 1199: WT-With Tumor; 1190: WT-With Tumor | 1190 → 1199 | Source order is not chronological; repeated same-day label collapses cleanly. |
| B | 191: TF-Tumor Free; 773: WT-With Tumor | 191 → 773 | Distinct response labels are retained as separate observed states. This association does not identify why the response changed. |
| C | 1881: WT-With Tumor; 1881: WT-With Tumor; 944: WT-With Tumor | 944 → 1881 | Same-day duplicate is collapsed and chronological order is recovered. |

## Limits

The verified reference point supports ordering by follow-up day for the eligible cases; it does not make the observations regularly spaced. Follow-up records are sparse and can represent routine visits, last contact, or event-driven submissions. A next-recorded-response benchmark therefore predicts a variable-horizon observed category. It is not a daily disease simulator, a causal treatment-effect estimate, or a validated clinical model. Diagnosis and treatment relative-day fields need their own source-field checks before they are joined into the same timeline.
